Convert data to another unit

Source: R/units.R
convert_unit.Rd

Converts a raster or a table to another unit of measure and records the new unit, so later steps read thresholds in the right unit.

Usage

convert_unit(x, to, from = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'SpatRaster'
convert_unit(x, to, from = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'c4e_tbl'
convert_unit(x, to, from = NULL, cols = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
convert_unit(x, to, from = NULL, cols = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A SpatRaster, a c4e_tbl or a data frame.

to

Unit to convert to.

from

Unit to convert from. Defaults to the unit recorded in x.

...

Unused.

cols

<tidy-select> Optional columns to convert instead of the base series. Indicator columns are still handled from the registry.

Value

x in the new unit, of the same class (a c4e_tbl for data frames).

Details

  • On a SpatRaster, the unit is read from terra::units() and written back; layer names and dates are kept.

  • On a c4e_tbl, the unit comes from the metadata. The base series is converted: the date columns of a wide table, or value in a long one. Indicator columns that are amounts are converted too. Percentiles are levels and take the full conversion. Excesses over a threshold are differences, so a K to C conversion leaves them unchanged. Counts of days and spell lengths never change. Numeric thresholds in the registry are converted, so day_abv_303.15 in K is recorded as a threshold of 30 C.

  • On a plain data frame, from is required; the result is a c4e_tbl.

Unit names are matched loosely: "degC", "deg C" and "Celsius" all mean "C", and "kg m-2 s-1" means "kg/m2/s". Rates per unit of time convert through their numerator: "kg/m2/s" to "mm/day" multiplies by 86400. Months and years have varying lengths, so "mm/day" to "mm/month" multiplies each value by the days in its month and needs monthly data.

See also

register_unit(), list_units()

Examples

tmax <- terra::rast(
  system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif", package = "c4e"))
terra::units(tmax)[1]
#> [1] "K"
tmax_c <- convert_unit(tmax[[1:3]], "C")
terra::units(tmax_c)[1]
#> [1] "C"

wide <- data.frame(ID = "1", X2022.01.01 = 300, X2022.01.02 = 305)
convert_unit(wide, "C", from = "K")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#> # Context:  value [C], wide; key ID
#>   ID    X2022.01.01 X2022.01.02
#>   <chr>       <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 1            26.9        31.9
